claim_ceiling: Abiotic laboratory-generated iron-mineralized chemical-garden structures and their artificial-maturation response; not evidence of natural occurrence or a universal morphology baseline

source.title: Tricks of Nature From the Ancient Earth and Early Mars: Chemical Gardens Generate Biomorphs With High Preservation Potential
source.article_license_note: The authors state that a CC BY license was applied to the Author Accepted Manuscript version. This does not automatically license unpublished raw images, measurement tables or derived data. Obtain and record artifact-specific terms.
source.supporting_information: gbi70045-sup-0001-FigureS1-S4.docx; includes SEM photomicrographs and EDS/XRD supporting figures; obtain from publisher and verify file-level rights before redistribution.

Supporting information gbi70045-sup-0001-FigureS1-S4.docx is listed by the publisher and contains SEM photomicrographs and EDS/XRD figures; direct download was unavailable during this research pass.

scientific_scope.natural_occurrence_statement: The paper says iron-mineralized chemical-garden formation has not been directly observed in nature; occurrence is predicted in some far-from-equilibrium geological settings.
scientific_scope.primary_lookalike: Hollow iron-mineralized biomorphic filaments that resemble microbial extracellular sheaths and some putative microfossils.
scientific_scope.procedure_naturalism: The authors explicitly state that the laboratory production procedure is not geochemically naturalistic. The paper does not demonstrate that these chemical gardens have formed in nature; it notes plausible settings and existing natural structures that have been proposed as chemical gardens.

reaction.post_reaction_wash: replace with distilled water by pipetting three times
reaction.drying: room temperature and pressure; approximately 3 days

sealed_tube.atmosphere: anoxic; frozen with liquid nitrogen and flame-sealed under vacuum

artificial_maturation.pressure_note: Estimated from water vapor pressure, assuming gas production from garden material is negligible.

measurement_rules: If a filament exceeded the field of view, a lower magnification was used.
Only structures clearly exhibiting filamentous morphology were measured.
For branched structures, the longest branch length was measured.
For variable-width filaments, maximum width was measured.

sample_hierarchy.inference_rule: Resample or split at the highest independent physical preparation/treatment unit, not at filament or image level. If only one tube exists per temperature, this source cannot support an independent held-out-temperature generalization claim.

eds.instrument: Oxford Instruments EDS integrated with SEM

unheated: Dominated by tubular hollow filamentous material and globular seed-grain envelope remnants.
Some filaments show consistent external diameters and circular cross-sections.
Branching and anastomosis occur; some structures vary in diameter and have tapered ends.
after_maturation: Filamentous material remains clearly discernible in most samples treated at temperatures up to and including 300_C.
At 300_C, roughly spheroidal 0.5-2.5 micrometre structures were observed, often coating filaments.
At 350_C, material is dominated by bulbous/botryoidal structures; traces remain but complete filaments are not clearly discernible.
The authors report relatively limited degradation compared with analogous biological material and inhibited transformation of ferrihydrite to crystalline iron oxides, likely influenced by silica.

biologic_comparator.claim: The authors state that analogous biological sheaths could not be observed after maturation at 280_C, whereas chemical-garden filaments remained discernible at 300_C.
biologic_comparator.caveat: This comparator is not representative of all biological structures, and cross-study sample sizes and preparation replication must be verified before quantitative classifier training.

quantitative_morphology.statistical_caveat: The article reports independent two-tailed Student's t-tests across n=300 filaments. Because the number of independent physical treatment replicates is not stated and observations are nested within images/tubes, OLI must not interpret the filament-level p-values as replicated treatment-level inference without author confirmation.

mineralogy_by_temperature.unheated: Two broad peaks associated with poorly crystalline two-line ferrihydrite; no crystalline silica peaks observed (amorphous silica may be present).
mineralogy_by_temperature.50_to_250_C: Ferrihydrite peaks persist; crystalline silica phases not observed.
mineralogy_by_temperature.300_C: High-intensity cristobalite and tridymite peaks; two low-intensity peaks tentatively identified as haematite. Iron phase cannot be confidently established due likely overlap with silica peaks.
mineralogy_by_temperature.350_C: Cristobalite and tridymite observed; no iron-bearing XRD phase confidently observed. EDS indicates iron-rich filament remains/cross-sections, but full morphology is difficult to discern.

benchmark_tasks.question: Can a morphology-only detector distinguish the laboratory abiotic chemical gardens from the biological comparator?
benchmark_tasks.anti_leakage: Split by preparation batch and sample, not by image crop or individual filament.

benchmark_tasks.question: Can a detector distinguish abiotic chemical-garden filaments from biological material after matched maturation conditions?
benchmark_tasks.anti_leakage: Never split by individual filaments or image crops. The independent unit is the preparation batch / reaction vessel / maturation tube. Temperature-held-out tests are admissible only if multiple independent tubes/batches per temperature are available; otherwise report leave-one-temperature-out as descriptive stress testing, not an independent generalization estimate.

benchmark_tasks.question: Do mineralogy and elemental maps add discriminating value beyond morphology?
benchmark_tasks.anti_leakage: Keep correlated fields of view and spectra from the same physical sample within one split.

benchmark_tasks.question: How do limited field of view, magnification changes, image resolution and missing mineralogical measurements affect false-negative and false-positive rates?

data_admission.access_action: Request original data and measurement tables from corresponding author; record exact terms, file hashes and sample IDs before ingestion.
data_admission.note: Article methods and reported findings are source-pinned; underlying sample-level data have not been acquired.
data_admission.data_access_statement: Supporting data available from corresponding author upon reasonable request; request raw SEM images, ImageJ measurements, EDS maps/spectra, XRD patterns, instrument settings, sample/tube hierarchy and the exact biological comparator dataset.

experimental_unit_audit.tube_to_temperature_mapping: The methods state that seven tubes were used and the tubes were heated across seven temperatures. One tube per temperature is a reasonable reading, but this mapping and whether independent preparation replicates existed must be confirmed with the authors.
experimental_unit_audit.inferential_unit_warning: The 300 filament measurements are nested within one treatment sample and up to 50 image fields. They are not 300 independent biological/abiotic treatment replicates. Any OLI reanalysis must preserve image and sample nesting and must not use filaments as independent n for between-treatment generalization.
author_confirmation_required: number of independent chemical-garden preparation batches
number of independent tubes/reactors per temperature
whether 300 filament measurements per temperature come from one or multiple physical specimens
whether unheated baseline has independent preparation replicates
